content: Galathil: I see the Dragonborn’s pet housecarl still clings to him like a cheap tavern wench. Tell me, does your beloved Thane share your… vision of Skyrim, or does he merely tolerate your bleating, like one tolerates the stench of rotten fish at the docks? Lydia: Shut your twisted Bosmer mouth, you sewer-dwelling knife-ears! My Thane appreciates a Nord woman—loyal, fierce, and untainted by Thalmor-loving, tree-fondling weakness. Unlike whatever freak show you’ve sculpted into the mirror today. Galathil: Ah, the mating call of the brainless brute. How charming. I sculpt , you dull-witted milk-drinker. While you’re busy grunting and swinging that overcompensating sword, my patrons slink from my chair as entirely new people—smarter, prettier, and far less likely to die in a ditch defending some fool’s misguided prejudices. Lydia: Ha! Your “art” is just hacking up faces for cowards and sneak-thieves. Meanwhile, I’ve split more Thalmor skulls than you’ve had hot meals. And my Thane? me—every night, in every way. Bet your wrinkled hands can’t say the same.

Galathil: How... quaint. Enjoy your barbaric rutting while it lasts, housecarl. Sooner or later, even brute warriors grow tired of brute companions. Lydia: Hah! Keep carving faces in your piss-stinking cistern, corpse-toucher.

(The location is now The Ragged Flagon.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Daegon, Lydia, Serana, Vex, Brynjolf) (MJR: What do you want?; Galathil: Hmm, I suppose I can work with your face. After all, the sculptor cannot always choose the finest clay. MJR: What are you talking about?; Galathil: I assumed you were here to see me about your face. To have it sculpted into something more... artful than Nature has bestowed upon you. MJR: What do you do?; Galathil: So are you here as a client? Shall I remake your face? MJR: I'll have to think about it.; Galathil: Indeed. It is no small thing to submit yourself to the flesh sculptor's knife.)

Tonilia: That one seemed uncertain about your services, Galathil. Can't say I blame him—there's something unnerving about letting someone carve into your face. Galathil: Most walk away thinking it over. Few return. But those who do understand that beauty is a weapon sharper than any dagger I've seen you carry. Tonilia: Sharp enough to cut through a mark's coin purse, I suppose. Still, at this hour, most of the folks stumbling in here aren't looking for a new nose—they're looking for a drink to forget their troubles. Galathil: Trouble and transformation often go hand in hand. A new face can be a new life, after all.

Tonilia: That view... reminds me of the passage out to the old Solitude Lighthouse. I always wondered what it'd be like to carve a new life out of stone and sea. Galathil: The Rock may be indifferent to our desires, but a face can be coaxed into anything you wish.
(The location is now The Ragged Flagon.) (Characters nearby (from nearest to furthest): Karliah, Lydia, Serana, Tonilia, Vekel the Man)

Daegon: This place smells worse than the Ratway, and that's saying something. At least there's ale. Galathil: Ale dulls the senses, but a sharp face cuts deeper. Have you reconsidered my offer from before? A new visage could serve you well in this cold land.
Daegon: Looks like Karliah's on the move again. Probably off to stab someone for a septim or two. Galathil: Purpose gives a face its true beauty. Perhaps you should follow her.

Daegon: Dirge looks like he's been chewing on a troll's boot for breakfast. At least he's consistent. Galathil: Some faces are born of hardship, their lines tell stories of survival. Would you like yours to tell a different tale?
Daegon: I've got enough stories carved into my skin already, thanks. Don't need a new face to go with them.
